restaurant_name: ศูนย์ทันตกรรม สมภพ-อัมพุช
text:
Today, I called the clinic to confirm my appointment time.
A: I asked about the orthodontist's available dates and times.
B: We don't have any appointments.
A: I was confused for a moment and asked if there were really no appointments scheduled, and if the doctor had any other available dates. (I asked this just in case, because I don't like asking too often.)
B: I informed them of the dates and times the doctor was available.
A: Okay, I'll call you back.
A: I looked up the information and confirmed that there really was an appointment on... so I called again to confirm whether there was an appointment or not. I told the staff about it. After some back and forth,
B: Oh, the next appointment is in May.
A: I was even more confused. What's going on? I emphasized to the staff again that I wanted an appointment on...
B: Oh, I'm sorry. It's today at this time.
A: Okay, thank you. (I hung up.) Three minutes later, I received a call.
B: I'm sorry, but the doctor has an appointment scheduled for... instead. The doctor isn't available on...
A: I was starting to get annoyed, so I asked what the real situation was. What day is it exactly? Be sure.
B: Sorry, my computer is acting up!!
A: Completely bewildered!! Blaming the computer, unless you are blaming yourself, huh?

restaurant_name: ศูนย์ทันตกรรม สมภพ-อัมพุช
text: The staff at the counter were very unpleasant. They work in customer service, but their expressions were like they were forced to sit there. Appointments were frequently rescheduled, sometimes even canceled just days before the scheduled date, wasting valuable preparation time. The queuing system was constantly delayed and never on time. Even with ample time allocated, we still wasted time waiting. The checkout process was incredibly slow; I once waited for an hour. It's truly only suitable for people with plenty of free time. They often give customers stern looks, especially regarding pricing, which isn't cheap. Sometimes their tone is so condescending that they make you glare at their colleagues. Is this what you call appropriate customer service? Customers are asking politely, and a polite response with a pleasant tone and demeanor isn't difficult. From the reviews I've read, I understand this isn't just my problem, but if you're going to improve anything, please start with the staff. There's no need to constantly glare at customers; it creates a negative atmosphere and intimidates customers. Please read the reviews and make improvements. From a 2.6-star rating, improvements would definitely make things better.

restaurant_name: ศูนย์ทันตกรรม สมภพ-อัมพุช
text:
Choosing the right dentist is crucial for effective treatment. I went to this clinic because of severe tooth sensitivity and certain decay, but the dentist said my tooth was fine and only did a scaling. They didn't even recommend an X-ray. Upon further examination, the X-ray revealed more than five cavities, some nearing the nerve, requiring referral to a specialist. The dentist even blamed me for delaying treatment, despite my prior warnings. Fortunately, the specialist diagnosed root canal treatment as unnecessary.

The front desk staff were terrible, treating me like I was receiving free service despite the clinic's relatively high prices.

The waiting list is extremely long. While I can tolerate this as I chose the clinic, the worst I've experienced is a cancellation half a year in advance, or an hour before the scheduled time. While this has happened four times before, with such short notice, it's unacceptable. Appointments for corrective treatment often take at least a month to process. Even after explaining the previous issues, the dentist shows no empathy for the patient's inconvenience.

This review isn't meant to pressure the clinic into making changes, as they likely won't, but rather to provide information for those considering a clinic.

Choosing the right dentist is essential for successful treatment.
The services are similar to a government hospital.
The prices are higher than average.

text: The doctor's attitude was extremely rude. I need to explain that the doctor came to warn me to brush and floss better before my next appointment, but I had already brushed my teeth that morning and only drank coffee. To be honest, there might have been some areas I didn't fully attend to, which is why I came to see the doctor. But let me put it this way: being a doctor is a service profession. If you look at it from another perspective, imagine you go to a car wash and the attendant tells you not to step in the mud, and next time, remember to rinse it off before washing. I have to ask, you have the brains to pass the medical entrance exam, but you can't even think like that? My girlfriend and I received exactly the same service, but the prices were different. I also had gum disease treatment, which wasn't any different from my girlfriend's, but I paid 500 baht more. Excellent service! If there was an option to give 0 stars, I would. Even giving 1 star felt outrageous.
